title: stc session anchors, v2
description: Per-session clock and geometry anchors, written by the helper. t0Ns is boot-relative nanoseconds at session start, as a decimal string because boot-relative ns can exceed 2^53 (~104 days of uptime) and JSON numbers travel through IEEE doubles. All other times in the session are relative to t0Ns. Adds an optional camera track in phase 3.

timebase.description: mach_timebase_info at helper startup. displayTimeNs = displayTime * numer / denom.

originX.description: global display-space origin of the captured display, in points (CGEvent coordinates are global)

firstFrameNs.description: Session-relative ns of the first captured frame, measured by the helper. The file carries the same offset only as an empty edit quantised to the movie timescale, so this is the exact value to check a recovered offset against.

camera.description: Absent means no camera track was even attempted. present:false means a camera was attempted (or considered) but yielded no track — measurement fields are meaningless then and must be omitted, not fabricated. Only present:true requires them.

frameIntervalNs.description: median inter-frame delta; the transform bounds the track end with it

stop.description: Present after a clean stop. t is session-relative ns.

reason.description: Why the recording ended, as the helper writes it. Four families, all of which reach this field: a stop the user or the app asked for ('user'); a stop the helper decided on ('display-reconfigured', 'stream-stopped', 'stopped-during-start'); a shutdown that ended a live take (STC-304) — 'quit', 'stdin-closed', or 'signal-N' for the signal number, which is why this is not a closed enum; and reserved values nothing writes yet ('device-lost', 'error'). A '-timeout' suffix on ANY of them means the writer did not finalise in time and the sidecars were written anyway — display.mp4 may be incomplete; CaptureSession.stop appends it to whatever reason it was given, so the suffix is a property of every family rather than a fixed list. helper/test/stop-reasons.test.ts holds this schema to the reasons the Swift can actually produce.
